learn.hook: Chintu fills a bucket with a big glass. Mintu uses a small glass. Who needs more glasses?
points: A bigger glass holds more, so FEWER big glasses fill a bucket.
A smaller glass holds less, so MORE small glasses are needed.
To compare two containers, fill each and pour into same-sized glasses. The one that fills more glasses holds more.
Use words: holds more, holds less, holds the most, holds the least.

example.q: A jug fills 6 glasses. A bottle fills 4 of the same glasses. Which holds more?

learn.reallife: At a wedding, big pots of water are poured into small glasses to serve guests.

games.title: Least to most
games.prompt: Each fills this many same glasses: cup 1, bottle 3, jug 5, bucket 20

games.title: More or less?
items: A bigger glass needs fewer fills.
Containers that look tall always hold more.
A tall thin glass may hold less than a wide bowl.
Pouring into same-sized glasses is a fair way to compare.
The same unit is used for both.
The container that fills the fewest glasses holds the most.

quiz.q: Chintu's glass is bigger than Mintu's. Who needs fewer glasses to fill a bucket?
quiz.explain: A bigger glass holds more, so fewer are needed.

quiz.q: A pot fills 8 glasses. A jug fills 5 of the same glasses. How many more glasses does the pot fill?
Bottle A fills 7 cups, bottle B fills 9 cups and bottle C fills 4 cups. Which holds the MOST?
quiz.explain: 9 cups is the most.

quiz.q: Same bottles (7, 9, 4 cups). Which holds the LEAST?
quiz.explain: 4 cups is the least.

quiz.q: To compare a bottle and a jug fairly, what should we pour them into?
quiz.explain: The same-sized glass is a fair unit.

quiz.q: A tank fills 20 big buckets or 40 small buckets. Which bucket holds more?
quiz.explain: Fewer big buckets are needed, so each holds more.

quiz.q: A tall, thin glass and a short, wide bowl. How can we be sure which holds more?
options: Fill one and pour into the other
quiz.explain: Pouring tests it. Height alone can fool us.

quiz.q: Jug fills 6 glasses. Pot fills twice as many. How many glasses does the pot fill?

teach.ask: Gappu has a big leaf cup and a small leaf cup. Which fills the pond bowl with fewer trips?
teach.praise: The big cup holds more, so I need fewer trips! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which cup holds more each time?

learn.hook: A bucket or a cup: which one would you use to fill a bathtub? Let's compare how much things hold!
points: Capacity is how much a container can hold.
We can compare by filling one container and pouring it into another.
We can measure with small cups or glasses: a jug may hold 6 glasses of water.
Litre (L) is the standard unit for liquids like milk, water and oil.
Small amounts are measured in millilitres (mL). 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.

example.q: A bucket holds 10 mugs of water. A pot holds 4 mugs. How many more mugs does the bucket hold?

learn.reallife: Milk comes in 1 litre and half-litre packets, and water bottles are often 1 litre.

games.title: Less or more than a litre?
Little to large
games.prompt: Holds the least to holds the most

quiz.q: Which of these holds the MOST water?
quiz.explain: A bucket is much bigger inside than a cup, spoon or glass, so it holds the most.

quiz.q: Which unit do we use to measure milk?
quiz.explain: Liquids like milk are measured in litres.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the unit for weight with the unit for liquids

quiz.q: One jug of water fills 5 glasses. How many glasses do 2 jugs fill?
quiz.explain: 2 jugs fill 5 + 5 = 10 glasses.

quiz.q: How many millilitres are there in 1 litre?
quiz.explain: 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.

quiz.q: Riya's bottle holds 2 litres of water. She drinks 1 litre. How much water is left?
quiz.explain: 2 litres − 1 litre = 1 litre.

quiz.q: A water tank holds 50 buckets of water. 20 buckets are used. How many buckets of water are left?
quiz.explain: 50 − 20 = 30 buckets are left.

quiz.q: Kabir pours a full bottle of water into an empty mug, and the mug overflows. What does this tell us?
options: The mug holds more than the bottle
The bottle holds more than the mug
quiz.explain: The mug could not hold all the water from the bottle, so the bottle holds more.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the container that overflows holds more

quiz.q: Half a litre is how many millilitres?
quiz.explain: 1 litre is 1000 mL. Half of 1000 is 500.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 litre is 100 mL, so half is 50

teach.ask: Gappu has a cup and a jug. He wants to know which holds more water. How can he find out?
teach.praise: Fill one and pour it into the other! Now I know the jug holds more.
teach.nudge: What can I do with the water to compare them?

learn.hook: How many ladles of dal fill one glass? Guess first, then pour!
points: Guess how many small containers fill a big one, then check by pouring.
The smaller the measuring vessel, the more times you must fill it.
If 1 jug fills 4 glasses, 3 jugs fill 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 glasses.
If 1 glass takes 5 ladles, 4 glasses take 20 ladles.
Choose a suitable vessel: a ladle to serve dal, a jug to pour water, a bucket to water plants.

example.q: 1 glass takes 3 ladles. How many ladles for 4 glasses?

learn.reallife: In a langar or a school mid-day meal, food is served with ladles of the same size so everyone gets the same.

quiz.q: 1 jug fills 4 glasses. How many glasses do 3 jugs fill?
1 glass takes 5 ladles. How many ladles for 4 glasses?
A bucket is filled with a mug and with a glass. The glass is smaller. Which needs more fills?
quiz.explain: A smaller vessel needs more fills.
quiz.mistake: Thinks small vessels need fewer fills

quiz.q: Raju guessed 6 cups fill a jug. When he poured, it took 8 cups. How far off was his guess?
Which is best to serve dal at lunch?
quiz.explain: A ladle serves a small amount neatly.

quiz.q: 18 glasses of water are needed. 1 jug fills 6 glasses. How many jugs?
A pot holds 10 bowls of rice. A bowl holds 2 ladles. How many ladles fill the pot?
quiz.explain: 10 bowls × 2 ladles = 20.

quiz.q: Bottle A fills 3 glasses. Bottle B fills 3 cups. Can we say they hold the same?
options: No, glasses and cups may be different sizes
quiz.explain: We can compare only with the same unit.

teach.ask: Gappu fills his water bowl with a tiny cup and his friend with a big cup. Who pours more times?
teach.praise: The tiny cup holds less, so I pour more times! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which cup holds less each time?

learn.hook: Why does the milkman use a measuring can, not just any glass?
points: Glasses are of different sizes, so a milkman uses a standard measure to give everyone the same amount.
A litre (L) is a standard unit to measure liquids like milk, water and oil.
Some containers hold more than 1 litre (a bucket), some less (a glass), some exactly 1 litre (a 1-litre bottle).
Estimate first: a bucket may hold about 10 litres. Then check with a 1-litre bottle.
Save water: reuse bottles and close taps. Every litre counts!

example.q: A bucket is filled using a 1-litre bottle 12 times. How much does it hold?

learn.reallife: Milk packets, oil bottles and water cans are sold in litres.

quiz.q: Why does a milkman use a measuring can?
options: So everyone gets the same amount
quiz.explain: A standard measure gives a fair, equal amount.

quiz.q: Which is measured in litres?
quiz.explain: Litres measure liquids.

quiz.q: Which holds MORE than 1 litre?
quiz.explain: A bucket holds many litres.

quiz.q: Which holds LESS than 1 litre?
quiz.explain: A glass holds much less than a litre.

quiz.q: Tina guessed her bucket holds 10 L. She poured in 1-litre bottles 13 times to fill it. How far off was she?
A family uses 6 litres of water in the morning and 8 litres in the evening for plants. How much in all?
Which is a good way to save water?
quiz.explain: Closing the tap saves many litres.

quiz.q: A water can holds 20 L. How many 1-litre bottles can it fill?
quiz.explain: Each bottle takes 1 L. 20 L fills 20 bottles.

teach.ask: Gappu asks why we use litres and not just cups. What would you say?
teach.praise: Cups are different sizes, but a litre is the same for everyone! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Are all cups the same size?

learn.hook: A 1-litre bottle poured into 2 equal bottles gives 2 half-litres!
points: Half a litre is one of 2 equal parts of a litre.
A quarter litre is one of 4 equal parts of a litre.
2 half-litres make 1 litre.
4 quarter-litres make 1 litre.
2 quarter-litres make a half litre.

example.q: How many quarter-litre cups fill a 1-litre jug?

learn.reallife: Milk packets often come in half-litre size. Small juice packs are about a quarter litre or less.

quiz.q: How many half-litre bottles make 1 litre?
quiz.explain: Half + half = 1 whole.

quiz.q: How many quarter-litre cups make 1 litre?
quiz.explain: 4 quarters = 1 whole.

quiz.q: How many quarter litres make half a litre?
quiz.explain: 2 quarters = 1 half.

quiz.q: Mummy buys 3 half-litre packets of milk. How many litres is that?
quiz.explain: 2 half-litres = 1 litre, plus 1 more half.

quiz.q: A jug holds 2 litres. How many half-litre glasses can it fill?
quiz.explain: Each litre fills 2 half-litre glasses. 2 + 2 = 4.

quiz.q: A 1-litre bottle is poured into quarter-litre cups. 3 are filled. How many more cups are needed to empty it?
Which is more: half a litre or a quarter litre?
quiz.explain: Half is 2 quarters, so it is more.

quiz.q: Raju drinks 2 quarter-litre glasses of milk. How much milk is that?
quiz.explain: 2 quarters = half.

teach.ask: Gappu has a 1-litre jar and quarter-litre cups. How many cups will the jar fill?
teach.praise: 4 quarter-litres make 1 litre, so 4 cups! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many quarters make a whole?

learn.hook: Hold a book in one hand and a pencil in the other. Which hand feels pulled down?
points: Hold one object in each hand. The heavier one pulls your hand down more.
Record your results: write which object in each pair is heavier.
On a pan balance, we can weigh things using coins, erasers or matchboxes filled with sand as units.
A pencil box that balances 12 coins is heavier than a sharpener that balances 3 coins.
Arrange objects from lightest to heaviest. Move books between bags to make two bags about the same weight.

example.q: Bag A has 5 books and bag B has 3 books (all the same). How can you make them equal?
steps: Move 1 book from A to B.
example.answer: Move 1 book from A to B

learn.reallife: Vegetable sellers use a pan balance with weights to sell sabzi.

games.title: Lightest to heaviest
games.prompt: Balances with coins: feather 1, pencil 3, book 20, water bottle 40

quiz.q: Riya holds a brick in one hand and a sponge in the other. Which hand goes down more?
quiz.explain: The brick is heavier, so it pulls down more.

quiz.q: A pencil box balances 12 coins. A sharpener balances 3 coins. How many more coins does the box weigh?
A pan balance shows a ball and 8 erasers balancing. A toy balances 5 erasers. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: 8 erasers is more than 5.

quiz.q: Which units are good for weighing small things on a pan balance?
quiz.explain: Same-kind coins weigh the same each, so they are a fair unit.

quiz.q: Order from lightest: mango 10 coins, guava 7 coins, papaya 30 coins.
Bag A has 6 books and bag B has 2 (same books). How many books should move from A to B to make them equal?
quiz.explain: 6 + 2 = 8, so 4 each. Move 6 − 4 = 2.

quiz.q: Kabir records: 'Bat or ball? Bat heavier. Shoe or sock? Shoe heavier.' How many pairs did he record?
quiz.explain: Bat-ball and shoe-sock: 2 pairs.

quiz.q: A matchbox of sand balances 1 eraser. A book balances 9 matchboxes. How many erasers does the book balance?
quiz.explain: Each matchbox = 1 eraser, so 9 matchboxes = 9 erasers.

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know if a nut or a berry is heavier, but he has no balance. What can he do?
teach.praise: Hold one in each claw: the heavier one pulls down more! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How can my claws help me compare?

learn.hook: Is a big balloon heavier than a small stone? Let's put them on a balance and see!
points: Weight tells us how heavy something is.
On a balance, the heavier side goes down and the lighter side goes up.
Big things are not always heavier! A balloon is big but very light.
Kilogram (kg) is used to weigh things like rice, vegetables and people.
Light things are weighed in grams (g). 1 kilogram = 1000 grams.

example.q: On a balance, a bag of potatoes goes down and a packet of chips goes up. Which is heavier?

learn.reallife: The sabziwala weighs vegetables in kilograms, and the jeweller weighs gold in grams.

games.title: Heavy or light?
items: The heavier side of a balance goes down.
The heavier thing pulls its side down.
A big balloon is heavier than a small stone.
Size does not decide weight. The stone is heavier.
1 kilogram is the same as 1000 grams.
We buy rice by weight, in kilograms.
A feather is heavier than a brick.
A brick is much heavier than a feather.

quiz.q: On a balance, which side goes down?
quiz.explain: The heavier object pulls its side of the balance down.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger object always goes down

quiz.q: Which of these is the heaviest?
quiz.explain: A brick is made of hard, packed clay, so it is much heavier than the others.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about how heavy things feel when lifted

quiz.q: Which unit is used to weigh a sack of rice?
quiz.explain: Weight is measured in kilograms. Litres are for liquids.
quiz.mistake: Uses the unit for liquids to measure weight

quiz.q: How many grams make 1 kilogram?
quiz.explain: 1 kilogram = 1000 grams.

quiz.q: Meena buys 2 kg of onions and 3 kg of potatoes. What is the total weight?
quiz.explain: 2 kg + 3 kg = 5 kg.

quiz.q: A balloon and a marble are put on a balance. The marble's side goes down. Which is lighter?
quiz.explain: The lighter side goes up. The marble went down, so the balloon is lighter.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bigger thing must be heavier

quiz.q: Arjun weighs 25 kg. His little sister weighs 15 kg. How much heavier is Arjun?
quiz.explain: Find the difference: 25 kg − 15 kg = 10 kg.

quiz.q: A bag of atta weighs 5 kg. Nani Maa uses 2 kg to make rotis. How much atta is left?
quiz.explain: 5 kg − 2 kg = 3 kg.

teach.ask: Gappu thinks his big fluffy pillow must be heavier than a small stone. How can he check?
teach.praise: The stone side went down! Big things are not always heavy.
teach.nudge: What tool can I use, and what does it show me?

learn.hook: A 1 kg packet of salt. Is your school bag heavier or lighter than that?
points: Things at home that weigh 1 kg: a 1 kg packet of sugar, atta or salt.
Guess if something is lighter or heavier than 1 kg, then check on a balance with a 1 kg weight.
Half a kilogram is half of 1 kg. 2 half-kilograms make 1 kg.
A quarter kilogram is a quarter of 1 kg. 4 quarter-kilograms make 1 kg; 2 quarter-kilograms make half a kg.
About half a kg: a small papaya. About a quarter kg: a big apple or a large onion.

example.q: A shopkeeper puts two half-kilogram weights on one pan. What weight is that?

learn.reallife: Vegetable shops use 1 kg, half kg and quarter kg weights every day.

quiz.q: Which is likely to weigh about 1 kg?
options: A packet of sugar marked 1 kg
quiz.explain: The packet is marked 1 kg.
quiz.mistake: Picks something too light or heavy

quiz.q: Which is HEAVIER than 1 kg?
quiz.explain: A big watermelon weighs a few kilograms.

quiz.q: Which is LIGHTER than 1 kg?
quiz.explain: An eraser weighs very little.

quiz.q: How many half-kilograms make 1 kg?
quiz.explain: Half + half = 1.

quiz.q: How many quarter-kilograms make 1 kg?
quiz.explain: 4 quarters = 1 whole.

quiz.q: How many quarter-kilograms make half a kilogram?
quiz.explain: 2 quarters = 1 half.

quiz.q: Mummy buys 1 kg of tomatoes using only quarter-kg weights. How many weights does the seller use?
quiz.explain: 4 × quarter kg = 1 kg.

quiz.q: A small papaya balances a half-kg weight. Two such papayas weigh about…
quiz.explain: Half + half = 1 kg.

teach.ask: Gappu's mother asks for half a kilogram of seeds. The shop has only quarter-kg weights. What should Gappu do?
teach.praise: Use 2 quarter-kg weights. 2 quarters make a half! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How many quarters make a half?

learn.hook: The milkman, the grocer and the water tanker all need maths. Let's solve their puzzles!
points: We add litres to litres and kilograms to kilograms.
Always write the unit with the answer, like 5 L or 8 kg.
Read the story: 'in all' means add and 'left' means take away.
To find how many small jugs fill a big bucket, count equal groups.

example.q: A milkman has 20 litres of milk. He sells 12 litres. How much milk is left?

learn.reallife: At home, we buy oil in litres and flour in kilograms, and we use maths to know how much is left.

quiz.q: A dairy has 30 litres of milk. It sells 18 litres. How much milk is left?
quiz.explain: 'Left' means take away. 30 − 18 = 12 litres.

quiz.q: A water cooler holds 4 litres. It is filled 3 times in a day. How much water is that?
quiz.explain: 3 times 4 litres: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 litres.

quiz.q: Harpreet buys 5 kg of rice and 2 kg of sugar. How many kilograms is that in all?
quiz.explain: 'In all' means add. 5 kg + 2 kg = 7 kg.

quiz.q: Riya fills a 10-litre bucket using a 2-litre jug. How many jugfuls does she pour?
quiz.explain: Count by 2s to 10: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. That is 5 jugfuls.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 2 from 10 instead of making groups of 2

quiz.q: A shopkeeper has 25 kg of potatoes. He sells 10 kg in the morning and 5 kg in the evening. How much is left?
quiz.explain: Take away both amounts: 25 − 10 = 15, then 15 − 5 = 10 kg.
quiz.mistake: Takes away only the morning sale

quiz.q: Kabir's mother bought 3 bags of flour. Each bag weighs 5 kg. What is the total weight?
quiz.explain: 3 bags of 5 kg: 5 + 5 + 5 = 15 kg.

quiz.q: A tank had 40 litres of water. 15 litres were used to water the plants. How many litres are left?
quiz.explain: 40 − 15: take away 10 to get 30, then 5 more to get 25 litres.

quiz.q: Which of these should be measured in kilograms?
quiz.explain: Apples are solid things, so we weigh them in kilograms. The others are liquids, measured in litres.

teach.ask: Gappu has 9 litres of water and uses 4 litres. He wrote the answer as '5 kg'. What went wrong?
teach.praise: Water is measured in litres! The answer is 5 litres. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Is water measured in kilograms or in litres?

learn.hook: Three balls look the same, but one is heavier. You may use the balance only ONCE. Can you find it?
points: Put one ball on each pan and keep the third aside.
If one pan goes down, that ball is the heavy one.
If the pans balance, the ball kept aside is the heavy one.
To order 3 balls from heaviest to lightest, compare two at a time and keep track of the results.
If A is heavier than B, and B is heavier than C, then A is heavier than C.

example.q: Balls P, Q, R. P goes down against Q. Q goes down against R. Order them heaviest first.

learn.reallife: Detectives and scientists use clever tests like this to find the odd one with few tries.

games.title: Balance puzzles
items: If the pans balance, the two balls on them weigh the same.
With 3 balls and one heavy, one weighing is enough.
Put one on each side, keep one aside.
If A is heavier than B and B is heavier than C, then C is heaviest.
The pan that goes up has the heavier ball.

quiz.q: Three balls, one is heavier. You put ball 1 and ball 2 on the pans. They balance. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: Balls 1 and 2 weigh the same, so the heavy one is the one kept aside.
quiz.mistake: Thinks there is no heavy ball

quiz.q: Three balls, one is heavier. Ball A goes down against ball B. Which is heavier?
quiz.explain: The side that goes down is heavier.
quiz.mistake: Picks the ball that went up

quiz.q: How many times must you use the balance to find the heavy ball among 3?
quiz.explain: One weighing is enough with the trick.
steps: One on each pan, one aside
quiz.mistake: Thinks you must try each pair

quiz.q: P is heavier than Q. Q is heavier than R. Which is lightest?
quiz.explain: P > Q > R, so R is lightest.

quiz.q: X is lighter than Y. Z is heavier than Y. Order from heaviest.
quiz.explain: Z > Y and Y > X, so Z, Y, X.

quiz.q: If pans balance with ball M on one and ball N on the other, what is true?
options: M and N weigh the same
quiz.explain: Balanced pans mean equal weight.

quiz.q: The pan with ball K goes UP. What does this tell us about K?
quiz.explain: The lighter side goes up.

quiz.q: A > B and A > C. Can we tell which of B and C is heavier?
options: No, we must weigh B and C
quiz.explain: We only know A is the heaviest. One more weighing compares B and C.

teach.ask: Gappu has 3 nuts and one is heavier. He can weigh only once. What should he do?
teach.praise: One on each pan, one aside! If they balance, the aside nut is heavy! Chirp!
teach.nudge: What should I do with the third nut?
